h1:
Hat Yai Cafes
12 Great Spots for Coffee, Brunch, Photos & Work
intro: Hat Yai isn't just dim sum and early-morning eats. Over the past few years the city's cafe scene has grown a lot — specialty coffee roasters who roast and brew with care, brunch spots where one plate fills you up, prettily styled rooms made for photos, and places with plugs and Wi-Fi for long work sessions, spread across both downtown and the area around Prince of Songkla University (PSU). We picked 12 spots that Hat Yai locals actually go to, and tell you which kind of visit each one suits.

blocks.html: Hat Yai's cafes split roughly into two zones: downtown around Niphat Uthit Road, Thamnoonvithi, and the commercial district, and the PSU area around Prince of Songkla University, full of student-priced spots and places built for working. Each cafe has its own character — some you go to for the coffee, some for the photos, some to open a laptop and sit all day. So we grouped them by what you're after, with rough prices updated from real reviews.

blocks.title: Read before you go
blocks.html: Prices in this guide are approximate ranges from reviews. Most drinks in Hat Yai run around 60–100 THB. Cafe opening and closing times change often, especially weekly days off, so check the shop's page again before you head out. At the spots we flag as good for working, expect bigger crowds during student exam periods (roughly May and October).

blocks.text: 12 Hat Yai cafes locals actually go to

items.name: Better Together Café & Bistro
items.blurb: The downtown cafe people think of first when it comes to working in Hat Yai. It has a separate co-working room, bookable meeting rooms, and savory dishes like pasta and rice for lunch. Quiet enough to sit all day, with plugs and Wi-Fi ready to go. Freelancers and students are regulars here.
items.meta: Downtown Hat Yai · co-working zone + meeting rooms

items.name: Specs on Specialty Coffee
items.blurb: For serious coffee people, this is the one. The focus is specialty beans, roasted and brewed with care, with both espresso and pour-over by bean. The drink people talk about is the orange-and-yuzu coffee, fresher than your usual latte. The room is clean and modern — good for sipping quietly or doing a bit of light work.
items.meta: Downtown Hat Yai · specialty coffee focus

items.name: The Company Coffee
items.blurb: A popular spot where people queue for the house-made fruit pies — blueberry, strawberry, and apple. The coffee is solid. It's busy almost all the time, so it suits an afternoon pie-and-coffee stop more than a long work session, since tables turn over fast.
items.meta: Downtown Hat Yai · known for fruit pies

items.name: KRANE
items.blurb: An industrial-loft style cafe with dark-roast coffee and fresh-baked goods, with both indoor and outdoor seating. The raw, cool tone photographs well, and people like that it isn't overly sweet like the usual minimalist cafe. Good for chilling with friends or taking photos.
items.meta: Hat Yai · loft style with outdoor seating

items.name: Photograph
items.blurb: A Japanese-feeling cafe with a clean, simple tone. The standouts are the basque cheesecake and the drip coffee. It suits anyone who likes quiet, easy-to-shoot corners that don't need much styling. Open morning to afternoon — good for a light brunch and a slow coffee.

items.name: Namkee Cafe
items.blurb: A clean, minimalist cafe near the bus terminal area. The desserts people order are the chocolate lava cake and the lemon cake. The space is open and airy, comfortable to sit in — good for a mid-day break. Closed Thursdays.
items.meta: Bus terminal area, Hat Yai · open ~08:30–17:00 · closed Thu

items.name: Hood
items.blurb: A vintage-toned cafe whose draw is its unusual drinks you don't often find — sugarcane coffee and coconut coffee. There are soft matcha cookies to snack on too. Good for anyone who likes trying new menu items and vintage photo corners.

items.name: Cafe La Sirene
items.blurb: A mermaid-themed cafe in clean white tones that photographs well from every angle. The house-made items people praise are the éclairs and croissants. Open daily, late morning to evening — good for photos and a bakery-and-coffee sit-down.
items.meta: Hat Yai · open daily ~09:00–18:30 · mermaid theme

items.name: Dham-má-daa
items.blurb: A warm-toned cafe whose name ("ordinary") sums up the mood — simple but comfortable to sit in, with well-made basic coffee and desserts. People drop by to read or chat over a bit of work. It's less crowded than the famous spots, so it suits a day when you want quiet.

items.name: Baroffee Cafe
items.blurb: A coffee shop downtown locals stop by regularly. The drink menu is wide, both coffee and non-coffee, with snacks to order alongside, and prices are easy on the wallet. Good for meeting friends or a short work session.

items.name: Lorem Ipsum Space
items.blurb: A clean-toned cafe space designed for sitting a long time, with long-table corners that suit spreading out a laptop. Workers and students come to open their work here. The mood is calm and low-noise — good for a day when you really need to focus.
items.meta: Hat Yai · designed for long stays

items.name: Seek Nature Hatyai
items.blurb: A green-garden-toned cafe for anyone who likes a touch of nature in the city — lots of plants, breezy seating, with good bakery and coffee. Good for photos in the garden corners and a long afternoon sit.

blocks.text: Pick a cafe by what you're after

blocks.html: If you're not sure which one to go to, start from your main purpose. Each Hat Yai cafe is good at a different thing — some are for the coffee alone, some for working, some for photos. Look at these three groups and pick the one that fits your day.

items.name: For specialty coffee
items.blurb: Specs on Specialty Coffee and KRANE focus on the beans and the brew. If you want coffee that takes flavor seriously, start with these two.

items.name: For working
items.blurb: Better Together and Lorem Ipsum Space have plugs, Wi-Fi, and tables made for a laptop. You can sit a long time without feeling pressured.

items.name: For photos & brunch
items.blurb: Cafe La Sirene, Photograph, and Seek Nature are prettily styled and shoot well, with bakery and desserts to pair with your coffee.

blocks.text: PSU-area cafes vs downtown — what's the difference

blocks.html: These two zones give different vibes. Choose based on which side you're staying on and the atmosphere you want.

items: PSU area — around Prince of Songkla University, with student-priced spots where drinks start a touch cheaper than downtown. Many places are two floors, with plugs at every table upstairs for reading and working. The crowd skews young and gets lively in the evening after class.

Downtown Hat Yai — around Niphat Uthit Road, Thamnoonvithi, and the commercial district, with more design-forward spots: specialty cafes, brunch places, and proper co-working rooms. Easy to reach if you're staying at a hotel in town.
Opening hours — most cafes open late, around 08:30–10:00, and close in the evening 17:00–19:00. Fewer stay open into the night, so if you want to sit late, check the closing time first.
Weekly day off — many close one weekday, like Wednesday or Thursday, not the weekend. Check the shop's page before you go to be sure.

blocks.title: Tips for working
blocks.html: If you're coming for a long work session, avoid the 14:00–17:00 weekend window when crowds peak. Co-working spots like Better Together fill up fast then. Try arriving at opening time or on a weekday for better, quieter corners. And bring an adapter in case there aren't enough plugs when it's busy.

Hat Yai cafes are friendly on the wallet compared to Bangkok. Most drinks run around 60–100 THB. If you order one coffee and one dessert, it works out to roughly 120–180 THB per person. PSU-area spots run a little cheaper since they cater to students, while specialty cafes or brunch places that also serve savory food push the budget up to around 200–300 THB per person. If you're working all day, it's polite to keep ordering a bit more as you go.

faq.q: Which Hat Yai cafe is best for working?
faq.a: Better Together Café & Bistro downtown is the most recommended for working, with a separate co-working room, meeting rooms, and plugs and Wi-Fi ready to go. Another is Lorem Ipsum Space, designed for long stays. In the PSU area, several two-floor spots have plugs at every table upstairs, also good for reading and working.

faq.q: Which Hat Yai cafe has genuinely good coffee?
faq.a: If you want specialty coffee that's serious about beans and brewing, go for Specs on Specialty Coffee and KRANE, which roast their own dark roast. Photograph stands out for drip coffee paired with basque cheesecake. All three suit people who come mainly to drink coffee rather than just take photos.

faq.q: What time do Hat Yai cafes open?
faq.a: Most open late, around 08:30–10:00, and close in the evening 17:00–19:00. Few stay open into the night. Many have a weekly day off mid-week, like Wednesday or Thursday, so check the shop's page before heading out, especially if you're set on a particular spot.

faq.q: How much per person at a Hat Yai cafe?
faq.a: Most drinks run around 60–100 THB. If you order a coffee and one dessert, it's roughly 120–180 THB per person. PSU-area spots are a little cheaper since they cater to students, while specialty cafes or brunch places that also serve savory food push up to around 200–300 THB per person.

faq.q: Which Hat Yai cafe is good for photos?
faq.a: Cafe La Sirene's white mermaid theme shoots well from every angle, Photograph has a clean Japanese style, and Seek Nature has green garden corners. If you prefer a raw, cool tone, go for KRANE's industrial-loft style and Hood's vintage feel.
